job.does: Checks new hackathon submissions in your sheet against your requirements, marks each Passed or Rejected with reasons, and sends you a summary.
job.done: Every new submission has a Status and Reasons, and you have the summary.

settings.label: Your submissions sheet
settings.help: The tab the submissions arrive in, one per row.

steps.title: Find new submissions
steps.plain: Read the submissions sheet and pick out the ones not checked yet
steps.description: Read the tab settings.submissions_sheet. New submissions are rows whose Status is empty: return submissions, each { row: its _row, project: the Project column, demo: the Demo column, notes: the Notes column }, and checks, one per submission and requirement in settings.requirements: { submission: its place in submissions, project, demo, notes, requirement }.

steps.title: Judge each requirement
steps.plain: Judge every requirement of every new submission: met or not met
steps.prompt: Does this submission meet this requirement, from its project, demo and notes?

steps.title: Count and mark
steps.plain: Count the requirements each one met, and mark it Passed, or Rejected when fewer than half are met
steps.description: For each submission count the verdicts (by item, matching checks) that are met. Rejected when fewer than half of its requirements are met, else Passed; Reasons lists the requirements not met. Return status_updates as sheets.update's arguments { sheet: settings.submissions_sheet, updates: [{ row, values: { Status, Reasons } }] } and summary { text } naming every submission and its result. With no submissions, return both as null.

steps.title: Write the results
steps.plain: Write Status and Reasons into each submission's own row

steps.title: Send the summary
steps.plain: Send you a summary of the run on Telegram

actions.description: Write Status and Reasons into each submission's own row
Send you a summary of the run
